prerequisites: Basic knowledge of analog and digital electronics, acquired in previous courses.
Familiarity with general concepts of programming and control logic is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and capacities to apply the scientific and technological fundamentals of industrial communication networks.

syllabus_topics: Basic Principles of analog and digital communication networks.
OSI Model for Industrial Networks. Fieldbuses.
The CAN (Controller Area Network) communication bus.
Buses and protocols in home automation, building automation and digital home.
Advanced instrumentation systems. Interfaces and electronic control. Smart sensors and actuators. Sensor networks. SCADA systems. USB bus and others.
Other fieldbuses and industrial communication and control applications.
teaching_methods: Autonomous and sequential study of contents
Continuous assessment activities oriented to analysis and decision-making
Non-presential laboratory practice (traffic analysis with Wireshark)
Integrative Final Project (design of a complete OT industrial architecture)

Use of the virtual course and support resources (methodological orientations, complementary materials, PEC indications, laboratory practice resources, final project resources, architecture examples, notices, forums for doubts)
Preparation for the in-person exam by solving exercises and previous exams
assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained by the weighted sum of the in-person exam (55%), three continuous assessment tests (5% each), the laboratory practice (5%), and the integrative final project (25%). For the continuous assessment, laboratory practice, and final project grades to be included in the final grade, a minimum score of 4.0 points must be obtained in the in-person exam. If the score in the in-person exam is less than 4, the final grade will only be the exam score. A final grade of 5.00 points or higher is required to pass the course. Continuous assessment grades are only valid for the current academic year.
